subject: Running simulated datasets on same model

messages.author: 87db6da4a9a8d291
messages.subject: Running simulated datasets on same model
parts:
Dear Nimble experts,

Please forgive my naive questions and lack of coding skills. I am new to Nimble, and I am trying to fit 100 simulated datasets (67x100) on one model. I am curious how to fit them under Nimble environment. I appreciate any hints and suggestions. 

very simple ICAR model:

ICARCode <- nimbleCode(
  {
    for (i in 1:N){
     
      O[i] ~ dpois(mu[i])                                # Poisson for observed counts
      log(mu[i]) <- log(E[i]) + alpha + phi[i]
     
      SIR[i] <- exp(alpha + phi[i])                      # area-specific SIR
      resSIR[i] <- exp(phi[i])                           # area-specific residual SIR
      e[i] <- (O[i]-mu[i])/sqrt(mu[i])                   # residuals      
    }
   
    # ICAR
    phi[1:N] ~ dcar_normal(adj[1:L], weights[1:L], num[1:N], tau.phi, zero_mean = 1)
   
   
    # Priors:
    alpha ~ dflat()                                      # vague uniform prior
    overallSIR <- exp(alpha)                             # overall SIR across study region
   
    tau.phi ~ dgamma(1, 0.01)                            # precision of the ICAR component
    sigma2.phi <- 1/tau.phi                              # variance of the ICAR component
   
  }
 
)

ICARmodel<-nimbleModel(code=ICARCode, constants=constant, data=cancerdata, inits=lstinits)

* cancerdata contains 67x100, where 67 is the number of counties, and 100 is the 100 simulated datasets.

Many thanks,

Best,
Vicky

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Running simulated datasets on same model
parts:
Dear Vicky,

Sounds interesting.  Each of constant, cancerdata, and Istinits should be a named list.  It sounds like you have cancerdata as an array.  The names of the list elements for any of those three arguments should correspond to variable names in your model code.

From your description, I think you would want data = list(O = cancerdata[1:67, 1]), so that you build the model with one data set to start.

After you build and compile the model and MCMC algorithm, you can assign new values to any data variables.  For example, if you have done

compiled_ICARmodel <- compileNimble(ICARmodel)

then you can do 

compiled_ICARmodel$O <- cancerdata[1:67, 2]

to set the values of O in the model to your second data set (if I follow).  To do this, the sizes (N and L in your model) must not change.  If they change, you would need to re-do nimbleModel and compileNimble.

For further steps and nimble basics, I'll refer you to our user manual at r-nimble.org.  It looks like you're just getting started and so that might be useful for you.  Let us know further questions.

-Perry
